items.q: Are you a city rec center?
items.a: No. We're a private commercial sports facility — not tax-subsidized, so pricing isn't in line with schools or rec centers. The municipal option is the Aurora Southeast Recreation Center.

items.q: Where are you and how do I get in touch?
items.a: 14200 E Alameda Ave, Suite 400, Aurora, CO 80012. Email admin@boomtownvb.com.
Hours vary by sport, program and season. Check current drop-in info before you visit.
Yes — parking is free and plentiful on-site. It's an active city lot, so lock your car and keep valuables out of sight; the facility isn't responsible for vehicles.

items.q: Can I bring outside food or drink?
items.a: No outside commercial food or drink (including coffee). Oda Up restaurant & bar and the Oda Up Bar serve food and drinks. Paid catering is the exception.
There is no lost & found — items are disposed of after events for sanitation. Electronics and valuables are not the facility's responsibility.
Yes — drop-in volleyball runs on a weekly-changing schedule. Confirm current times before visiting.
Yes — Boomtown runs youth (≈9–16) and adult volleyball training.

items.q: How do I book a court or turf?
items.a: Through Boomtown events. As a commercial facility, individual court rentals are very limited and priced as event-day rates.

items.q: I lost my personal ball — can you find it?
items.a: The facility isn't responsible for personal balls or equipment.

items.q: Can I host an event or birthday?
items.a: Yes — it's a commercial venue. Birthdays are very limited (Saturday nights); corporate and daytime events are easier to schedule. Book through the Event-Den.
Yes — through Boomtown (and USAV RMR). Book ~6 months ahead; a rental agreement must be signed and paid in full before the event.

items.q: How do I sponsor or partner?
items.a: Email admin@boomtownvb.com. Youth-access donations go through the Colorado Athletics Foundation.

specs: Studios: yoga floor, dance foam floor, dance carpet floor
safety: No weapons or firearms. Only player backpacks enter the building; purses and camera bags must be open for inspection.
No gum. No sports drinks, coffee or tea in playing areas — only sealable, clear water. No Stanley cups (no cap = spill hazard).
No standing on tables or bar tops; no climbing nets, fences or sprinklers. Children must be supervised at all times.
No personal/camping chairs or coolers on the courts; court chairs are not to be moved. Floor mats/seats are fine if they don't scratch.
No athletic trainer or ice on site — bring your own first-aid kit (kits/bandages sold for a fee).
No appliances plugged in. Phone charging is allowed around the bar areas.
No ball handling outside authorized event areas — no dribbling or throwing balls elsewhere.
Don't roam into other athletic areas or construction zones (soccer field, lounge, med-spa, dance studios).
No pets except service animals (12 hours' written notice required); service animals aren't allowed on playing surfaces.
No outside commercial food or drink anywhere (including Starbucks). Alcohol stays in the bar seating area.
Keep all food and drink off the courts. Teams clean their space or are fined; spills must be cleaned immediately.
No tables or camping in front of the building (Aurora camping ban). Eat outside food in your vehicle; no tailgating or littering.
There is no lost & found — items are disposed of after events.
rules.rmr: RMR players only may bring a brown-bag lunch carried in a player backpack; if it doesn't fit the backpack, it doesn't enter. Spectators may not bring bags (purses/camera bags excepted) or food. Doors open 7:00 AM; coaches' meeting 7:30 AM at the admin desk. Coaches must check out with the site director or scores aren't entered (auto-forfeit).
fines: 1st offense — $25 charge to the offending club/team
2nd offense — $50 charge to the offending club/team
3rd offense — team asked to leave, forfeits remaining matches, not welcomed back
rules.amenity: On-site sports-therapy massage with in-house therapist Lena Chon — limited spots, usually sold out. Free guest Wi-Fi (login required).
